source.title: IEG: Robust Neural Network Training to Tackle Severe Label Noise
source.authors: Zizhao Zhang; Han Zhang; Sercan Ö. Arik; Honglak Lee; Tomas Pfister

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how validation accuracy changes as label-noise ratios rise, using a noise-robust training method with trusted data. The paper does not test the original random-label fitting setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation accuracy across label-noise ratios and training curves at 80% noise. It does not report fitting completely random labels with an unchanged standard training recipe. Training-time comparisons and results from cited prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study motivates a noise-robust training method using networks' tendency to memorize noisy labels. Its experiments evaluate mitigation through trusted data, reweighting, relabeling, mixup and consistency losses; they do not test the stated random-label fitting claims. Validation accuracy under this modified method does not establish perfect fitting of corrupted training labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that a small trusted set can guide exemplar weighting and relabeling to achieve strong robustness under severe label noise across several datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes meta reweighting and relabeling, trusted probe data, mixup, augmentation and a consistency loss; its reported training is not the original standard random-label setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise ratio, probe-set size, model architecture, consistency-loss weight k, augmentation policy, and whether mixup or relabeling is enabled affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed method retains high validation accuracy under uniform label corruption by using trusted labels and modifying training supervision.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trusted-data-guided reweighting and relabeling can improve classification robustness under severe label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: A larger consistency-loss coefficient suppresses late overfitting in the proposed method at 80% uniform noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Consistency regularization can reduce noisy-label overfitting within this trusted-data-based training framework.

record.problems: The reported accuracy results concern a custom noise-robust method using trusted labeled data, so they do not directly test the claim's unchanged standard-training setup. Most tables report validation accuracy rather than training accuracy. Training curves are figure-only and the text gives limited quantitative detail.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 separately reports Ours with 0.5k and 1k probe data across the same noise ratios; Table 1 also reports Ours with 0.01k and 0.05k probe data. These additional probe-size conditions were left out to prioritize the default 0.1k probe setting and ResNet29 comparison; they appear in Tables 1–2. Other noise types and datasets were left out because the version specifies random label corruption.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error and chance test performance on completely random labels with unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Time to fit true versus random labels and convergence time as corruption increases. Appendix C compares method overhead with vanilla training instead.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect fitting of corrupted training labels across a noise sweep together with steadily worsening test error toward chance. The reported sweep evaluates a method designed to replace or discount noisy supervision.
Whether weight decay, dropout and data augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms clean-label generalization.
Direct measurement of shared real patterns being learned before noisy labels. Delayed overfitting in a mitigation ablation and learned relabeling coefficients do not establish that learning order.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V4 limits_scope verdict: neither missing training-fit measurements nor mitigation performance establishes a boundary of V4. Excerpt E2 repeats prose values of 96.5% and 94.7%, which disagree with Table 1's default-method values of 96.2% and 93.7%; it therefore does not substantiate R4 or R8. Figure 3's caption assigns dotted lines to training and solid lines to evaluation, opposite Figure 2's convention.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment trains standard networks on completely random labels without trusted data or method changes.
The paper estimates its method's training time relative to vanilla training, but does not compare time to fit true versus random labels or sweep training time by corruption fraction.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiments.

The paper reports validation accuracy across several label-noise ratios and training curves at 80% noise, but does not establish perfect training accuracy across the full noise sweep or test error at chance under fully random labels.

Ablations vary augmentation and consistency losses in the proposed noise-robust method, not whether standard explicit regularizers permit random-label fitting or whether removing them harms clean-label generalization.
No comparison of learning order for real versus random labels over training.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Proposed method on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 with uniform label noise, reported probe-data settings
reader_labels.reason: Validation accuracy declines with increasing noise but remains well above chance at 80%; training-perfect fit across the sweep is not shown (R1–R16). At 80% noise, the paper says exceeding the expected average training accuracy can signal overfitting, and consistency-loss weight affects overfitting (R17–R19).
